images.caption: Charles Fort - Kinsale -Married Quarters Built for King Charles II in the 1670s the design is heavily influenced by the French engineer Vauban. The fort is a coastal protection to the approaches to Kinsale harbour. The fort was occupied by James II's forces in 1689 and recaptured by William of Orange's Dutch troops in October 1689. The recognised weakness with the fort was the landward side where it is overlooked by higher ground. The garrison surrendered once the outer wall had been breached by artillery fire. The fort was occupied until the Irish Civil War in 1921 when the Essex Regiment left.

images.filename: Charles Fort - Kinsale - Battery and Governor's House - geograph.org.uk - 1392386.jpg
images.caption:
Charles Fort - Kinsale - Battery and Governor's House Built for King Charles II in the 1670s the design is heavily influenced by the French engineer Vauban. The fort is a coastal protection to the approaches to Kinsale harbour. 
Wilful, the daughter of an early governor, Coloner Warender, married Sir Trevor Ashurst an officer at the fort. On their wedding night she admired some flowers on the rocks below. Her husband took over from a sentry who was went down to collect some flowers for the lady. This took some time and unfortunately the husband fell asleep and was shot for dereliction of duty at his post by the governor on his nightly round. On hearing the news Wilful threw herself off the battlements and is said to haunt the fort.

images.filename: Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale.jpg
images.caption: The Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale, Ireland. The Cunard passenger liner, RMS Lusitania, bound for Liverpool from New York, sank 12 miles (20 km) away, off the Old Head (the Old Head lighthouse can be seen in the photo at the top right), on 7 May 1915 after being torpedoed by a German U-boat during the First World War. 1198 of the ship's 1959 passengers and crew perished. The ruins of de Courcey castle can be seen in the middle-distance.
images.alt: The Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale, Ireland.
